distinguishing_features: Pressure-modulated conical seat that converts internal pressure into increased elastomer contact pressure.
FFKM elastomer as the primary sealing contact instead of an embrittlement-prone metal seat.
Spring preload combined with a pressure-coupled, high-stiffness Inconel 718 annulus mechanically decoupled from stem load.
Leak-rate bench validation at 100 bar H2 for 72 hours using a mass-spectrometer detector.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Reduce leakage in high-pressure hydrogen valve seats caused by metal-seat embrittlement and gas permeation while preserving seal integrity over the service interval.
parsed.viable_reason: FFKM is not an impermeable hydrogen barrier and the alleged squeezing out of permeated hydrogen is not a valid permeation-control mechanism, so the stack does not reliably prevent the stated permeation leak at 100 bar.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Although none of the cited arts teaches it, the candidate merely transfers a known self-energizing conical seal geometry and known hydrogen-compatible seal materials into the valve seat, which a skilled engineer would routinely try.
